chunks: Aban narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who said:

I asked him about a man who said to his slave, "If something happens to me, then he is free," while the man is obliged to free a slave as expiation for an oath or ẓihār. Is it permissible for him to free his slave—the one for whom he assigned emancipation if something happens to him—as the expiation for that oath?
He said: "It is not permissible—the one whom he has designated for that in this matter."

key_terms.تَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ: the freeing of a slave as a required legal expiation
key_terms.ظِهَارٍ: a prohibited form of declaration likening one’s wife to a forbidden relative, requiring expiation
key_terms.كَفَّارَةِ يَمِينٍ: the expiation due for breaking or violating an oath

ai.seo_question: Can a conditionally emancipated slave be used for kaffarah of an oath or ẓihār?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a slave who has already been designated for conditional emancipation upon the master's death or a similar event. It states that such a slave cannot be used to fulfill the separate obligation of freeing a slave for kaffarah of an oath or ẓihār, because he has already been assigned for another emancipatory purpose.
